title: The money too heavy to move

probes.question: How was ownership of a large rai stone established?
options: By its history in oral tradition

probes.question: True or false: rai stones were quarried mainly on Yap itself.

image.alt: A large round limestone rai stone with a central hole standing upright among palms and rocks on Yap

panels.text: On the island of Yap, in Micronesia, people used large stone discs called rai stones. They were quarried on several of the Micronesian islands, mainly Palau.
The stones were highly valued by the Yapese and used for important ceremonial gifts. The largest extant stone is 3.6 metres (12 ft) in diameter and weighs 4,000 kilograms.
Ownership of a large stone, which would be too difficult to move, was established by its history as recorded in oral tradition rather than by its location.
Some modern economists have viewed rai stones as a form of money: a demonstration that the value of some forms of money can be assigned purely through a shared belief in said value.
